narrative.overview: Ink on warm paper. The signed-in app is a quiet desk: a cream ground, blue-black ink text, hairline rules in sand, and a single deep teal that marks everything actionable or current. The photos supply all the color; the chrome stays out of their way.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, ink text, exactly one accent (deep teal).
Flat: shadows only on the avatar menu and drag tray (and a faint lift on the selection bar).
Small radii: 6px controls, 8px cards and panels.
Serif for headings of time and place; sans for everything operational.
Equal care for phone and desktop: sidebar becomes a bottom tab bar at 860px.

rules.name: The One Teal Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only accent. Status hues appear only to report state, never to decorate.

rules.name: The Photos Carry Color Rule
rules.body: Chrome stays paper, ink and teal so uploaded imagery is the most colorful thing on screen.

rules.name: The Serif Is For Time And Place Rule
rules.body: Serif is limited to brand name, day headings, page titles, auth card titles and album names.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Cards, panels, buttons and tiles carry no shadow. If a surface needs separation, give it a rule line or a tonal step.

dos: Do use teal (#1f6f6b) as the only accent and Pressed Teal (#17524f) for hover and current text.
Do keep controls at 44px minimum and radii at 6px (controls) and 8px (cards).
Do use the serif only for brand, day headings, page titles, auth titles and album names.
Do separate surfaces with 1px sand rules or paper tone steps.
Do draw icons from the shared 24px, 1.8-stroke inline set in currentColor.
Do say plainly when something cannot be verified or recovered; use brick for errors and moss for confirmations.
donts: Don't add shadows to cards, buttons or tiles; shadows belong to menus and the drag tray.
Don't introduce a second accent hue or tint the chrome with photo-derived color.
Don't use the serif for buttons, labels, menus or body copy.
Don't use external fonts, CDNs or icon fonts.
Don't draw the sealed-envelope mark anywhere beyond the logo and storage area.
